title: Quality delta charting components (CI bands, segment filters) + regression visual language
creator: Kenji Nakamura
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Goal
Define reusable charting components and a consistent visual language to represent quality deltas between control vs shadow variants during rollouts/experiments. This ticket focuses on:
- Delta charts that communicate directionality, magnitude, and uncertainty (confidence intervals)
- Segment filtering UI patterns that are cardinality-safe and consistent across Console
- Clear regression indicators + thresholds ("warn" vs "fail") that avoid false certainty

Context
Shadow traffic creates paired request sets (control response returned to user; shadow evaluated async). Results show quality metrics like refusal rate, format adherence, instruction following rubric score, etc. The UI needs to show:
- Absolute values for control and candidate
- Delta (candidate - control) in % points or score points
- Confidence intervals and sample size to prevent overreacting to noise
- Slice-and-dice across safe segments (region, request type, model family, route env) without exploding cardinality

Non-goals
- Defining the full create-experiment flow (DES-611)
- Writing the final UI copy/tooltips (DES-613)

Deliverables
1) Component specs (behavior + states)
A. Delta time-series chart (primary)
- Shows delta over time (default) with optional overlay of control & candidate absolute series.
- Y-axis: delta units (e.g., +pp for rates; +score for rubric).
- Centerline at 0; positive/negative area shading is subtle (not green/red fills) to avoid implying “good/bad” universally.
- CI band around delta line (95% default) using a translucent band.
- Interaction: hover shows time bucket, delta, CI bounds, n (paired samples), control value, candidate value.
- Handling missing data: gaps rather than connecting across missing buckets.

B. Delta snapshot chart (secondary)
- For “Last 24h / Last 7d” view: a point + CI whisker (dot-and-whisker) per metric.
- Supports sorting by absolute delta magnitude, and filtering to “Regressions only.”
- Includes n and “power insufficient” badge if below min sample size.

C. Metric row component (for tables)
- Left: metric name + info icon.
- Middle: delta value with direction arrow (up/down) and CI in tooltip.
- Right: control/candidate absolute values (compact).
- Optional: small sparkline of delta over selected window.

D. Regression callouts (advisory + gating-ready)
- “Regression suspected” state when:
  - threshold exceeded AND
  - CI does not cross 0 (statistically distinguishable at chosen confidence)
- “Inconclusive” state when CI crosses 0 or n below threshold.
- “Improvement” state is visually neutral; we avoid celebratory green to keep focus on risk detection.

2) Confidence / significance visual language
- CI band is always shown when available.
- We do not label as “statistically significant” in the UI; we label as:
  - “Directionally worse (high confidence)” when CI entirely below 0 beyond threshold
  - “No clear change” when CI overlaps 0
  - “Insufficient data” when sample size too low or scoring lag too high
- Provide user control for confidence level (90% / 95%) behind “Advanced” toggle for beta; default 95%.

3) Segment filters pattern (cardinality-safe)
Requirements
- Must align with observability constraints: only allow pre-approved dimensions and bounded enumerations.
- Filters must be shareable via URL and consistent across “Shadow Experiments” and Rollout timeline panels.

Proposed pattern
- Filter bar with up to 3 pinned facets:
  - Time window (Last 1h/6h/24h/7d, plus custom)
  - Segment (dropdown of safe dimensions)
  - Variant selector (Control vs Shadow A/B + “All shadows”)
- Segment facet behavior:
  - Step 1: choose dimension (Region, Request type, Route env, Customer tier (internal only), Model family)
  - Step 2: choose value(s) from server-provided list; no freeform text.
  - Step 3: optional “Compare segments” (max 2) to overlay two delta series (guarded; defaults off)
- “Add filter” is capped (max 2 additional facets) to keep queries fast and reduce cognitive load.
- For long lists (e.g., routes), we use “Top 20 by volume” + search within those; no arbitrary route ID search in beta.

4) Threshold visualization
- Two horizontal lines on delta chart (optional):
  - “Warn” threshold (e.g., -1pp) as dashed line
  - “Fail” threshold (e.g., -3pp) as solid line
- Thresholds are metric-specific and come from backend (don’t hardcode). If missing, hide thresholds.
- On hover, thresholds display exact value and where it came from (default bundle vs user override).

5) States & edge cases
- Scoring lag: show banner within chart container if scoring is behind (e.g., “Scoring delayed by ~18m; latest buckets may be incomplete”).
- Streaming requests: if metric coverage is partial, show “partial coverage” badge in metric row.
- Sparse segments: show “insufficient data for this segment” and a suggestion to widen time range.
- Accessibility: CI band + line are distinguishable in grayscale; do not rely on red/green.

Design system notes
- Colors:
  - Neutral baseline: Slate line for 0.
  - Delta line: Indigo 600.
  - CI band: Indigo 200 @ ~30% opacity.
  - Regression markers: use Redwood “Signal” tokens (Amber for warn, Red for fail) only for threshold breach callouts/badges, not the entire series.
- Typography:
  - Delta values in tabular rows use tabular numerals.
- Units:
  - Rates always show “pp” (percentage points) to reduce confusion.

Data contract assumptions (to validate with ENG-5407 / telemetry)
For each time bucket and segment:
- control_value, candidate_value
- delta
- ci_low, ci_high (or standard_error + sample_size)
- paired_sample_count (n)
- coverage indicators (scored_count / mirrored_count)

Open questions
- Do we support multiple-comparison correction messaging when many metrics are displayed? (Proposed: no in beta; keep copy minimal; rely on thresholding + CI.)
- Do we default to delta-only view or show absolute overlay? (Proposed: delta-only default; absolute in a toggle.)
- What’s the default min n per bucket before we draw a line? (Proposed: backend decides; UI shows gaps.)

Acceptance criteria
- Component spec covers: visual examples, interactions, loading/empty/error states, and accessibility notes.
- Segment filters are bounded and map to known safe dimensions.
- Regression language avoids implying certainty when data is inconclusive.
- PM + Eng sign-off that the spec matches planned backend aggregates.

comments: 2026-01-07 (Kenji Nakamura): Drafted initial dot-and-whisker + delta time-series patterns. Key decision: avoid global green/red semantics for “improvement/regression” because some metrics are better when lower (refusal rate) vs higher (format adherence). Proposal: reserve red/amber only for threshold breaches, and encode direction with arrows + signed values.

2026-01-10 (Marissa Cole): +1 on neutral palette. For beta, we need at-a-glance “is this getting worse?” without reading tooltips. Please ensure the regression badge is visible in the table view and matches rollout guardrail language (warn/fail).

2026-01-16 (Sana Farid): CI display: recommend showing 95% CI by default, but avoid the phrase “significant.” Also please display n and a coverage ratio; we’ve seen cases where shadow scoring coverage drops and deltas look artificially stable.

2026-01-20 (Allison Grant): Segment filters must not allow high-cardinality values (route_id, prompt_id). Suggest UX only offers server-provided enumerations and clearly labels “Top by volume” vs “All.” Also ensure overlays cap at 2 to avoid unreadable charts.

2026-01-27 (Dylan Brooks): Implementation note: our charting library supports bands + threshold lines, but hover tooltips need a consistent schema. If we can standardize fields (delta, ci_low/high, n, control, candidate), we can reuse across charts.
2026-02-03 (Kenji Nakamura): Updated spec to include scoring lag banner + gap behavior for sparse buckets. Added explicit ‘pp’ unit for rate metrics and tabular numerals for delta display in tables.
2026-02-11 (Paula Mendes): Please align “fail” threshold visuals with rollout guardrails. Even if v1 is advisory-only, we want to avoid rework when auto-rollback is enabled later.
